hook: In simulations, trace atmospheric gases slow ice growth and thin the liquid-like layer on ice.
hook_turn: slow ice growth and thin the liquid-like layer on ice.
summary: Gases in cold air are usually treated as bystanders at ice surfaces. Molecular simulations show that every gas tested slows the ice front by sticking weakly at the water-ice interface, and after freezing they gather near the quasi-liquid layer and air boundary, passivating dangling bonds and thinning that layer. The work is simulation only, with no laboratory measurement of the effect.
title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure.
